questions.question: A debugging agent has read ten files and a long log. Most of its 14,000-token history is file contents it looked at once. What is the risk of simply cutting it down?
options: There is no risk; old file contents are never needed
It may fit afterwards but have lost the few specific facts (a port, a file:line) the next step depends on
The model will refuse to continue
questions.explanation: 'It fits' is not success. Recall of the needed facts is.

questions.question: What does clearing old tool results keep?
options: Every tool call (what was done) plus a stub saying how big the result was; the newest results stay in full
A summary written by the model
questions.explanation: The model can see what it did and call the tool again if it needs the output.

questions.question: The offline handoff note kept 'dates.py:88' but lost the port 5433. Why?
options: The port was in a newer step
The agent had written the crash location down with note(), but nobody wrote down the port, and the note writer didn't extract it
questions.explanation: A note keeps only what its writer chose to write. Agents that take notes as they go lose less.

questions.question: Why does the order 'clear, then write a note' lose facts?
options: The note writer then sees stubs instead of results, so it can't copy values that clearing removed
Notes can't be written after clearing
questions.explanation: Write the note from the full history first, then clear what the note covers.

questions.question: auto_compact with clear_first=True fitted the window after clearing and stopped. What went wrong?
options: It chose the free option, fitted, and lost every needed fact; size was the only check
questions.explanation: Automatic compaction should be tested on recall of planted facts, not only on size.

questions.question: A handoff note says the database port is 5432; the config says 5433. What is the lesson?
options: A model-written note can change specific values; ask it to copy values exactly, and test notes against the original run
questions.explanation: 5432 is the PostgreSQL default, so a model may 'correct' the real value toward it. Paraphrased values are wrong values.
